title: Failed resolution is non-atomic and soft-locks the game
expected: ven-148-166 is re-parsed at load (all-cards.ts:808-810) into `{type:"move", target:{unit,enemy}, to:"battlefield"}` (verified via bun). In riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/move.ts:530-541 a plain-string `to` that isn't a special keyword becomes targetZone="battlefield" and is passed straight to ctx.zones.moveCard; no such zone exists (zone-configs.ts only defines base/battlefieldRow/`battlefield-${id}` etc.). core operations-impl.ts:192-226 moveCard splices the card out of its source zone (line 203) BEFORE checking the target and throwing `Target zone battlefield does not exist` (line 225). These zone ops mutate engine.internalState directly (rule-engine.ts:487-490), which is outside the immer produce; the catch at rule-engine.ts:676-706 returns EXECUTION_ERROR without restoring internalStateBefore (snapshot at :565 is only used for undo). Net: unit removed from every zone, game state (chain item/priority) rolled back unchanged, so each subsequent pass/resolve re-throws the same error -> soft-lock; only undo/Rewind restores internalState (:1240-1242).
observed: After the failed resolve, the targeted enemy Recruit token disappeared from every zone (base [] and not in trash/banishment/any battlefield — 113 cards, none is the token), while the chain item stayed active with activePlayer=player-2; every subsequent passChainPriority returns the same EXECUTION_ERROR, UI shows 'Goldfish has Priority — waiting...' forever. Only Rewind recovers.
